recent_news: May 28, 2026: Raised $65B Series H at a $965B post-money valuation, co-led by Capital Group, Coatue, D1, GIC, ICONIQ and XN; funds earmarked for safety and interpretability research, compute expansion, and products and partnerships.

profile.summary: Anthropic is a San Francisco-based AI company founded in 2021, selling access to its Claude models via chatbot, API and agent tools such as Claude Code. It raised a $65B Series H at a $965B post-money valuation in May 2026 and reported a $47B revenue run rate. It has reportedly confidentially filed for an IPO, with a possible Nasdaq listing targeted for October 2026 (unconfirmed by the company).

profile.industry: Frontend cloud platform / developer platform and cloud infrastructure software
profile.business_model: Usage-based charges on compute, bandwidth and storage, plus per-seat Pro subscriptions and larger Enterprise contracts, while the free open-source Next.js framework drives adoption.

recent_news: July 2026: Vercel agreed to acquire Better Auth, the open-source TypeScript auth library, which stays MIT-licensed; its founder and core team are joining Vercel.
July 2026: Vercel acquired Egyptian-founded Stakpak, an open-source autonomous DevOps agent startup, for an undisclosed amount; the founding team is joining Vercel.
Press coverage describes the Stakpak deal as Vercel's third acquisition in about a year, following NuxtLabs in July 2025 and Better Auth in July 2026.

July 2026: Vercel launched a multi-year strategic partnership with the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS Formula One Team, with Vercel branding on race cars starting at the British Grand Prix and expanding from 2027.
Vercel and Globant announced a multi-year strategic alliance, with Globant-run AI Pods that modernize legacy frontends and ship AI-built apps to Vercel in one click.
June 2026: At its Ship conference in London, Vercel launched a new agent framework, full-stack capabilities and enterprise controls for its agentic infrastructure platform.
January 2026: Gel Data wound down and its team (led by Yury Selivanov) joined Vercel to invest in Python ecosystem support; Vercel said it was not commercializing the platform.
August 2026: Vercel appointed Amit Agarwal to its board of directors.
March 2026: Vercel appointed Mitchell Hashimoto to its board of directors.
A security breach at Vercel in April 2026 is cited as a risk by one secondary blog; not confirmed by a primary source.
deal_signals: Closed $300M Series F at a $9.3B post-money valuation on Sept 30, 2025, co-led by Accel and GIC; reported as oversubscribed.
Series F paired with a roughly $300M secondary tender offer for employees, former employees and early investors, providing liquidity.

Series F investors included BlackRock, StepStone, Khosla Ventures, Schroders, Adams Street Partners and General Catalyst (new), plus GV, Notable Capital, Salesforce Ventures and Tiger Global (existing).
Company-reported growth at Series F: user base doubled over the prior year and 82% top-line growth year over year.
Teams and Enterprise accounts make up more than 50% of v0 revenue (company disclosure at Series F).
Run-rate revenue of about $340M by end of February 2026, up from about $100M at the start of 2024; 84% year-over-year growth cited in March 2026.
CEO Guillermo Rauch signaled IPO readiness in April 2026 at HumanX but gave no timeline; the company has not filed.
Acquisition activity: Tremor (January 2025), NuxtLabs (July 2025), Better Auth and Stakpak (July 2026).
profile.summary: Vercel is a San Francisco-based frontend cloud and developer platform founded in 2015, known for maintaining Next.js and for AI products such as v0. It is privately held, last raised a $300M Series F at a $9.3B valuation in September 2025 alongside a ~$300M tender offer, and reported about $340M in run-rate revenue by early 2026. The CEO has signaled IPO readiness without a timeline, and the company has been actively acquiring startups and adding senior leaders and board members.

profile.summary: Datadog is a New York-based, Nasdaq-listed (DDOG) observability and security SaaS provider founded in 2010 with roughly 8,000+ employees. It is growing about 35% YoY with Q3 2026 revenue of $1.20 billion, raised FY2026 guidance, and is an active acquirer, with a reported ~$4 billion Upwind deal under consideration (unconfirmed). Key risks include revenue concentration after its largest customer reduced usage, a rich valuation, and a share price drop after Q3 earnings.
